organizer: Genç Başarı Eğitim Vakfı (Junior Achievement Türkiye)
eligibility_verbatim: Program targets '13-18 yaş grubu lise öğrencilerinin' (high school students aged 13-18). Students apply via an online form (selecting the 'student' role). Participants join in teams of 5-10 people and establish a small-scale company with zero capital through the GençBizz Portal, produce and sell a real product/service within school settings, and present financial reports to shareholders before liquidating the company at the end of the program; the program culminates in a 3-day national final.
turkey_access_reasoning: This is a Türkiye-based program run for Turkish high school students specifically; a Turkey-based student applies directly.
international_access_notes: Turkey-only; secondary sources mention participation in 'national and international fairs' as part of the experience, which could add an international-facing element to a student's profile.
team_or_national_delegation_required: Students form their own teams of 5-10 to found a company together; individual students apply as 'student' role and are grouped into ventures.
cost_notes: No cost found for student participation; program is delivered via teacher advisors and volunteer business mentors.

evidence.raw_excerpt: 13 – 18 yaş grubu lise öğrencilerinin ... Programa 5 -10 kişilik ekipleri ile katılan katılımcılar ... kendi küçük ölçekli şirketlerini sıfır sermaye ile kurdukları, okul sınırları içerisinde gerçek ürün / hizmet üreterek satış yaptıkları

notes_uncertainties: DUPLICATE-RISK FLAG FOR REVIEWER: Genç Başarı Eğitim Vakfı is Türkiye's Junior Achievement affiliate, and GençBizz's mechanics (student-run mini-company with zero capital, liquidated at year-end) are the classic global 'JA Company Programme' methodology. The live DB already has 'JA Company Programme (Europe)' and 'Young Enterprise Company Programme' (UK) as separate country-specific entries for what is structurally the same JA methodology, so we've treated GençBizz consistently as Türkiye's own distinctly-branded instance — but the next reviewer should double check it is not an unwanted third duplicate of the same underlying program before marking PRODUCTION_READY. This is explicitly NOT the same as the already-excluded 'GençBizzTech,' which is a separate, tech-focused sister program from the same foundation.

organizer: Roots & Shoots Türkiye (Jane Goodall Institute global network)
eligibility_verbatim: Roots & Shoots Türkiye was founded in 2020 as the Turkish chapter of Jane Goodall's Roots & Shoots, a program active in more than 70 countries (140+ globally per the parent organization) uniting children and youth around three impact areas: People, Animals and Environment, via a '4 Step Formula' project model. Site states 'anyone can join... individuals, to classrooms, to other community groups... find a group near you or start your own.'
eligible_grades: Preschool through university age (global program design); no Turkey-specific age floor confirmed
turkey_access_reasoning: This is Türkiye's own official chapter of the global Jane Goodall Institute network, confirmed via the organizer's own Turkish-domain site.
international_access_notes: Connects to a 70+ country global network; local project work is Turkey-based but the movement/branding is international and internationally recognized (Jane Goodall Institute).
team_or_national_delegation_required: None required; a student can join an existing group or start their own (typically as/with a school club).
cost_notes: No cost identified; standard Roots & Shoots model is free to join.

evidence.raw_excerpt: Join us to take part in the change! ... unites millions of children and young people in more than 70 countries ... People, Animals, and Environment
a domain where children and youth can meet people from different disciplines and acquire the necessary skills to develop projects ... 4 Step Formula

notes_uncertainties: Confirmed the Turkey chapter is real and official via two direct fetches of its own domain, but could not retrieve the specific 'Join Us' page content (age requirements, exact registration steps, whether an adult sponsor is required) — the link exists (rootsandshootsturkey.org/bize-katil/) but its content was not captured in our fetch (attempted, errored). Recommend a follow-up fetch of that specific page before marking VERIFIED.

eligibility_verbatim: Genç Kızılay is active in '81 il ve 150 üniversitede' (81 provinces and 150 universities). 'İlköğretim ve lise çağındaki öğrencilere Kızılay'ı tanıtıcı organizasyonlar yapılmakta' (introductory organizations are run for middle- and high-school-age students), and the organization works with school administrations to establish 'Gençlik Kolları' (Youth Branches) inside schools. General Türk Kızılay individual membership, separately, requires being 18+ ('18 yaşını dolduran her vatandaşımız'). Activities span disaster/emergency field support, social aid, education/awareness projects, youth camps (first aid, disaster awareness, social responsibility training), and participation in branch decision-making.
eligible_grades: Middle school through university (school-based Youth Branches make high school participation possible pre-18, even though formal branch membership requires turning 18)
turkey_access_reasoning: High-school-age participation is explicitly described (school Gençlik Kolları / awareness organizations for 'lise çağındaki öğrenciler'), but FORMAL individual membership in a Kızılay branch requires being 18+, so a younger high-schooler's access route is through a school-based youth branch rather than direct individual membership — this nuance should be surfaced to the student.
international_access_notes: Türkiye-based; internationally credible via affiliation with the global Red Cross/Red Crescent Movement (IFRC).
team_or_national_delegation_required: None; joins via school Youth Branch or (for 18+) direct branch membership via gonulluol.org.

evidence.raw_excerpt: İlköğretim ve lise çağındaki öğrencilere Kızılay'ı tanıtıcı organizasyonlar yapılmakta ve konferanslar verilmektedir. Okullarda Kızılay Gençlik Kolları kurulmasını ... okul idareleriyle işbirliği yapılmaktadır.

notes_uncertainties: The exact selection process and depth of real leadership responsibility available to a school-based Youth Branch member (as opposed to a full 18+ member) was not fully detailed on the pages reviewed — recommend the next researcher confirm with a specific school/provincial branch what concrete roles/responsibilities a 15-17 year old can actually hold before over-promising 'leadership' framing to students.

eligibility_verbatim: 'A child must be above 12 years and under 18 years of age, from anywhere in the world.' The child 'must have a clear history of standing up and fighting for the rights of children,' with changemaking efforts that led to 'a concrete positive result or impact on the rights of children locally, nationally or globally,' and 'the child must have agreed to be nominated.' A group of up to 5 children can be nominated together; organizations cannot be nominated.
turkey_access_reasoning: Eligibility is explicitly 'from anywhere in the world' with no country exclusion found.
international_access_notes: Global nomination-based prize; winner attends an international ceremony.
team_or_national_delegation_required: Individual or small group (max 5 children); nominee must consent to being nominated but does not nominate themself.

evidence.raw_excerpt: The International Children's Peace Prize honours young changemakers who stand up for children's rights ... Project Fund ... Desmond Tutu Study and Care Fund
A child must be above 12 years and under 18 years of age, from anywhere in the world ... the child must have agreed to be nominated for the International Children's Peace Prize

notes_uncertainties: Detailed eligibility text was captured via search-engine summary of KidsRights' own nomination guidance booklets rather than a direct successful fetch of that specific sub-page (two direct fetch attempts to guess URLs 404'd); the organization and prize themselves were independently confirmed via a direct fetch of kidsrights.org. Like the Diana Award, this requires finding a third-party nominator, not a self-application — worth flagging to students as a 'get nominated' rather than 'apply' opportunity.

canonical_name: Doğa Öncüleri (WWF-Türkiye Nature Pioneers Youth Programme)
eligibility_verbatim: Per secondary-source description of the organizer's own program: invites volunteer middle-school (grades 5-6-7) and high-school teachers and students to develop projects under mentor/teacher guidance in five tracks — 'Yaban Hayatı Korucuları' (Wildlife Protectors), 'Su Melekleri' (Water Angels), 'Plastik Avcıları' (Plastic Hunters), 'Gıda Savaşçıları' (Food Warriors), 'Karbon Tutucuları' (Carbon Capturers) — with a stated programme goal of 1,000 schools / 1,000 teachers / 10,000 middle- and high-school student project implementers. This differs from WWF-Türkiye's general adult volunteering track, which explicitly requires being 18+.
eligible_grades: Grades 5-7 (middle school) through lise (high school), per programme description
turkey_access_reasoning: Turkey-specific programme run by WWF's own Turkish national organization, explicitly for Turkish middle- and high-school students (distinct from the 18+-only general WWF-Türkiye volunteer track).
international_access_notes: Turkey-only; internationally credible via the global WWF network/brand.
team_or_national_delegation_required: Appears to be school/teacher-mediated (a volunteer teacher signs up the school/class) rather than a pure individual self-application, based on available description.

evidence.raw_excerpt: Doğa Öncüleri Gençlik Programı invites volunteer middle school (grades 5-6-7) and high school teachers and students ... Yaban Hayatı Korucuları, Su Melekleri, Plastik Avcıları, Gıda Savaşçıları, Karbon Tutucuları ... aims for 1,000 schools, 1,000 teachers, and 10,000 ... students

notes_uncertainties: IMPORTANT: our automated fetch tool was blocked (HTTP 403) on wwf.org.tr on two separate attempts (main program page and a related PDF), so this record is built from a search-engine summary of the organizer's own page content rather than a direct fetch/quote — treat as CANDIDATE, not VERIFIED, until a human or a different fetch method confirms directly on wwf.org.tr. Also confirm current-year application windows and whether an individual (non-school-affiliated) student can join, since the description suggests a teacher/school-mediated entry route.

canonical_name: Habitat for Humanity Global Village (Youth/Teen participation)
eligibility_verbatim: 'Teens 16 years and older can join our international efforts.' Trips run in '40 countries,' lasting 1-2 weeks, working 'alongside future homeowners.' Per Habitat's separate minor policy (found via search, not directly fetched): 'Minors aged 16 and 17 may participate in Global Village trips if they are accompanied by a parent or under care of an institution such as a Habitat affiliate, school or university,' with a ratio of 'no more than five minors to one adult,' and restrictions on roof work, power tools, blitz builds, and heavy lifting for minors.
turkey_access_reasoning: No citizenship/residency restriction was found on the official page ('no restrictions based on citizenship or residency are mentioned'), but practical access requires funding an international trip and mandatory adult/institutional accompaniment for a 16-17 year old, which a Turkey-based student would need to arrange (e.g. via a school group) rather than travel solo.
international_access_notes: Requires international travel to the host country/build site; not an online/remote opportunity.
team_or_national_delegation_required: Not required to join as a team, but a minor must be accompanied by a parent or an institution (school/university/Habitat affiliate) per the minor policy.
cost_notes: Not confirmed in sources reviewed; Global Village trips historically require participants to fund their own travel/trip fees (commonly four-figure USD range for similar international-build programs elsewhere), but we did not independently verify a current figure — do not present a specific number to students without reconfirming.

evidence.raw_excerpt: Teens 16 years and older can join our international efforts while immersing themselves in new cultures ... Our work spans the globe, from Argentina to Zambia ... 40 countries
Minors aged 16 and 17 may participate in Global Village trips if they are accompanied by a parent or under care of an institution ... no more than five minors to one adult

notes_uncertainties: Cost is a real and likely significant barrier that we could not pin down with a current number — flag to students as 'expect a substantial trip fee, confirm directly with Habitat before committing.' The mandatory-accompaniment rule for 16-17 year olds means this is realistically a 'join through your school' opportunity rather than an independent solo application for most students in that age band; only 18+ participants could plausibly go unaccompanied.

turkey_access_reasoning: This is Türkiye's own national scouting federation and official international WOSM/WAGGGS member — inherently Turkey-based and open to Turkish students through local scout groups.
international_access_notes: Internationally recognized via WOSM/WAGGGS membership; may open doors to international scouting jamborees/exchanges, not independently confirmed here.
team_or_national_delegation_required: Joins a local troop; advancing to any youth leadership role/course requires an active federation license (renewed annually).
cost_notes: A leadership course fee of approximately 300 TL was reported (secondary source) for one specific course; base scouting membership/license costs not confirmed.

organizer: Captain Planet Foundation, Lonely Whale, and Point Break Foundation (co-founders)
eligibility_verbatim: 'Age 11-18' youth 'looking for ways to fight ocean plastic.' Described as empowering 'existing and emerging youth leaders... to create their own campaigns to take action against ocean plastic pollution,' with curriculum modules such as 'Campaigning 101' and 'Making Your Pitch.' Has trained 'over 600 young ocean activists from 30+ countries' across past cohorts (e.g. 20+ countries and 32 US states in one cohort). At least one past edition ('this year') was explicitly 'virtual and free,' including room & board for accepted participants, with travel scholarships available.
turkey_access_reasoning: Past cohorts drew from 20-30+ countries, suggesting broad international eligibility, but no page we reached explicitly confirmed Turkey's inclusion or a current, open, non-region-limited cycle — some past editions were region-specific (e.g. a 'Caribbean Bootcamp').
international_access_notes: When run as a general/global cohort it has been virtual and free; some editions are region-specific (e.g. Caribbean-focused), so a Turkey-based applicant should confirm which specific cohort (general/global vs. regional) is currently open.
team_or_national_delegation_required: None; individual youth application, though participants often work in teams during the bootcamp itself.
current_cycle_label: Not confirmed for 2026/2027 — most detailed information found dates to 2019-2020 cohorts
cost_notes: Historically free (including room & board) for accepted participants in at least one cohort, with travel scholarships; not reconfirmed for a current cycle.

evidence.raw_excerpt: age 11-18 ... over 600 young ocean activists from 30+ countries ... virtual and (this year) free ... Lilly's Plastic Pickup ... the '345 Pledge' with Plastic Free Cayman

notes_uncertainties: Most concrete details we found (specific cohort sizes, countries, 'free' cost) date to 2019-2020 editions; we could not confirm this program is still actively running in 2026 with a current, open, globally-accessible (non-regional) application cycle, nor could we confirm a live application link. HIGH PRIORITY for next researcher: reconfirm current operating status directly before treating as production-ready — this may have paused, changed sponsors, or gone region-only since 2020.
